findings.description: The picker reads `$('keep').checked` separately for each file instead of capturing the choice when the selection begins. If a sender enables Keep details for a future selection while a large batch is still processing, later photos in the existing batch are sent with their original GPS data and no warning.
findings.title: Batch photos can leak GPS after a toggle

findings.description: `prepareFile` warns only when the sniffed bytes or the MIME type say HEIC. Any other file that isn't a JPEG goes through `if (!isJpeg(head)) return { file };` with no `warn`, even though the module header says HEIC, PNG, WebP and video are all "sent unchanged with a warning". The picker accepts `image/*,video/*`, so an iPhone or Android video (QuickTime `©xyz`/ISO6709 location atoms, `ftyp qt  `/`mp42`, neither in `HEIF_BRANDS`), a PNG with an `eXIf` chunk, or a WebP/AVIF with EXIF reaches everyone in the room with its location and the sender is never told (T-I5).
findings.title: Videos and PNG/WebP keep their GPS with no warning

findings.description: `keep()` copies every APP0 segment and every APP14 segment beginning with `Adobe` without checking whether either contains extra private data. A picked JPEG with location or other details in those segments is sent with those bytes intact and no warning, because `prepareFile()` treats the copy as successfully cleaned.
findings.title: Photo details can reach recipients

findings.description: `stripJpeg()` treats the standalone JPEG TEM marker as though it has a segment length and can return `null` when the following bytes are interpreted as that length. For a valid JPEG containing TEM before its end marker, `prepareFile()` consequently sends the original metadata-bearing file, albeit with a warning.
findings.title: Some valid photos retain their details

findings.description: The picker runs every picked JPEG through `prepareFile` with no option argument, and nothing in the diff or in `web/` reads a Keep details choice. A grep of `web/` finds no Keep details text and no checkbox, though the PR description says one was already wired in. A sharer who wants the original, as PRD US5 requires, therefore gets a cleaned file every time.
findings.title: Sharers cannot send original photos

findings.description: The PR description says the real-iPhone check of the picker's HEIC-to-JPEG conversion was not done and is deferred to S17, and nothing in the diff records a result. The only iPhone evidence is a synthetic fixture in `tests/jpeg-fixtures.mjs`, so the claim that iPhone photos lose GPS through the picker stays unverified.
findings.title: iPhone GPS result is never recorded

findings.description: `prepareFile` checks `/^image\/hei[cf]/i.test(file.type)` before it checks the content with `isJpeg(head)`. A file whose browser MIME type says HEIC (usually taken from its extension) but whose bytes are a JPEG skips `stripJpeg` and is sent with all its EXIF/GPS. The content could have been cleaned, but the user only gets a warning.
findings.title: A JPEG labelled as HEIC is never cleaned
